disposition_reason: Primary ICP-MS/ICP-OES measurements of nine elements in commercial bone broths, plus controlled bone-simmering experiments.

study.design: Controlled simmering experiments (acidity, bone type, species, cooking time) plus a survey of three commercial bone broth-based foods
study.origin: white and black pig bones raised in Taiwan; bovine bone imported from Australia (experiments); commercial broths of unstated origin
study.market: local meat market (bones); local stores in Douliu city, central Taiwan (commercial broths)
study.method: Hot-plate HCl/HNO3 digestion of 100 mL filtered broth; Pb, Cd, Cu, Cr by ICP-MS (ELAN DRC II); Fe, Zn, Al, Mg, Ca by ICP-OES (Optima 5100 DV)
lod: MDL ICP-MS: Pb 0.21, Cd 0.17, Cr 0.27, Cu 0.24 ppb; ICP-OES: Fe 10.9, Zn 11.5, Al 25.2, Mg 72.1, Ca 14.2 ppb
study.qa: Spike recoveries Pb 105.8, Cd 96.5, Cr 98.9, Cu 99.6, Fe 107.8, Zn 86.2, Al 109.3, Mg 94.3, Ca 94.6%; calibration with certified multi-element standards; no CRM

controls.control: Animal species of bone (white pig, black pig, bovine leg bone), acidified simmering
controls.outcome: Pb extracted at 12 h: 6.14 (white pig), 4.33 (black pig), 2.53 (bovine) ug/kg bone; differences not significant (p = 0.249)
Pb extraction did not change significantly with time (white pig 7.90 -> 6.14 ug/kg bone, p = 0.919); Ca and Mg increased significantly after > 8 h
Ca extraction x17.4 and Mg x15.3 on average; other metals increased except Fe and Zn; Pb values figure-only; Cd below MDL in all experimental samples

unresolved: Experimental broth results (Table 1, Figure 1) are total metal extracted per kg of wet bone, not concentrations in broth; recorded only as controls.
Commercial broth collection dates not reported.
Cd means (0.27-0.64 ppb) are close to the 0.17 ppb ICP-MS MDL; handling of results below MDL in means is not stated.

regulatory_or_exposure.value: Pb 1.5-2.1 ug/serving mean (max 5.2) vs 250 ug/day from WHO PTWI; Cd 0.1-0.3 ug/serving vs 70 ug/day ATSDR MRL
